title: AWS CWI Training in Las Vegas, NV: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Las Vegas structural steel, stadium, resort and data center welders: corporate, online or one-to-one. D1.1 code focus.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Las Vegas, Nevada: Six Days for Structural Steel and Special Inspection Welding Inspectors
html:
Welding in Las Vegas is mostly about putting steel up. The skyline is built and rebuilt in structural steel, from resort towers and convention halls to arenas and the new ballpark rising on the old Tropicana site, and the valley keeps adding data centers, substations, warehouses and road structures around it. Almost all of that steel is welded to AWS D1.1, and on permitted projects someone has to verify those welds for the special inspection record. That is why the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential carries weight in Southern Nevada. Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for the AWS CWI examination with a six-day (6-day) course spanning Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application, delivered in three formats: corporate, at an employer's facility; online, with an instructor answering questions; and one-to-one, online or in person. AWS administers the examination and is the body that certifies; Atlantis teaches the material and certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Las Vegas. Atlantis has offices in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India, and none in Nevada. To get started, send a Las Vegas CWI exam prep enquiry.

How the six days work for a Southern Nevada candidate

Each day of the course maps onto part of the exam. The opening pair of days handles Fundamentals, the material behind Part A: processes and their effects, AWS terms, joint geometry, welding and weld symbols, metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities, NDT methods, calculations, safety and the inspector's role. Day three is practical preparation with weld gauges, measurement and procedure documents. Day four lives inside your Part C code book. Day five puts you through timed practice papers, and day six closes gaps and walks through what happens between application and exam day. For the full breakdown, see the AWS CWI exam prep course page.

Corporate, for a contractor, fabricator or agency

A steel erector, fabricator or special inspection agency with several staff to prepare can have the six days run at its own facility. The practical work then uses that company's gauges and real welds, often connection mock-ups and rejected production pieces, and the code day concentrates on the D1.1 provisions the group meets on site.

Online, for individuals working site hours

Individuals study online from a plan built on the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers. An instructor answers questions in writing as they work. Because nothing is tied to a class schedule, the plan survives early summer starts, overtime near a topping-out and the irregular hours of field inspection.

One-to-one, for a single candidate

Six days of sessions between one candidate and the instructor, held online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It is the format for someone who wants every hour aimed at their own weak spots.

Where welding inspection work comes from in Southern Nevada

Las Vegas has little heavy process industry, so its welding inspection demand is shaped by construction and the infrastructure that supports a fast-growing valley.

The ballpark on the former Tropicana site

The Athletics' new stadium is going up on the Strip where the Tropicana stood until its demolition in October 2024. By June 2026 construction officials said the bowl steel had been completed in about three months and the first of five large roof trusses was in place, with a second steel truss arch lifted in August. Roughly 650 craft workers were on site in June, a number expected to more than double once interior and exterior work ramps up, and the team says the ballpark is on track to open before the 2028 season. A project like this is a concentrated lesson in structural welding inspection: heavy field connections, large trusses assembled from shop-welded pieces, erection sequences and the paperwork that follows every critical weld.

Resorts, casinos and entertainment venues

Resort construction never fully stops in Las Vegas. New towers, expansions and remodels bring structural steel framing, transfer girders, canopies, show rigging supports and large signage structures. Recent venues such as Allegiant Stadium and the Sphere were large structural steel jobs in their own right, and each new venue repeats the pattern of shop fabrication followed by intense field welding.

Data centers and the power behind them

Data center campuses have become a steady source of steel and pipe work around the valley. In June 2026 Clark County commissioners approved another Switch facility, known as LAS 19, in the Enterprise area of the southwest valley, connected to a substation the company built with NV Energy. Data center buildings bring structural frames, equipment platforms and pipe racks, and their closed-loop cooling systems bring welded mechanical piping, while each new substation and transmission line adds steel structures of its own.

Signs, canopies and specialty structures

Large signs and architectural steel features are part of the city's identity, and Clark County's building department has issued a code interpretation on the design and special inspection of signs, a reminder that sign structures can fall under special inspection too. Aluminum appears in facades and some sign structures, which is where AWS D1.2 comes in.

Roads, water and utilities

Highway structures, pedestrian bridges over busy corridors, water and wastewater facilities and utility pipelines round out the picture. Bridge steel follows AWS D1.5, pipeline welding follows API 1104, and plant piping falls under the ASME codes.

Special inspection in Clark County and the City of Las Vegas

Clark County builds to an amended version of the International Building Code, and Chapter 17 of that code governs special inspections, including steel construction. Special inspectors are hired by the owner, engineer or architect of record rather than by the contractor, and the building official approves their qualifications. The county's building department approves the special inspection agencies that do this work, and accreditation through IAS, the International Accreditation Service, plays a large part in how agencies show they are competent. The City of Las Vegas guidelines say a special inspection agency must be approved by the Clark County department before a permit is issued, that inspectors must display approved identification, and that agencies work to the county's technical guidelines, including TG-016 and TG-016A.

For steel fabrication the same guidelines tie shop work to approved fabricators. Where a fabricator is not approved by a recognized body such as AISC or IAS, the city requires third-party inspection at the fabrication shop under IBC Sections 1704 and 1705 and the AISC 341 and 360 standards. Those AISC standards set their own expectations for the qualification of welding inspection personnel, and agencies and fabricators commonly use the CWI to meet them. Clark County also publishes its own welder qualification record form. The practical upshot for a Las Vegas inspector is that the CWI is rarely the only document involved, but it is often the one an agency or fabricator puts forward to show a person is qualified to inspect structural welding.

Who hires CWIs in Las Vegas

  • Special inspection agencies. Agencies approved by Clark County staff field inspectors on high-rise, resort, stadium and data center projects, and structural welding is one of their core scopes.
  • Steel fabricators. Shops supplying the valley's projects keep in-house QC inspectors, and a fabricator without approved status invites third-party shop inspection, which raises the value of having qualified inspection in house.
  • Steel erectors and general contractors. Contractors use CWIs for quality control on field welding, welder qualification tracking and coordination with the special inspector.
  • Utilities, data center developers and owners. Owners hire inspectors to oversee contractors on substations, pipe work and equipment platforms.
  • Testing laboratories. Materials and NDT firms combine welding inspection with ultrasonic and magnetic particle testing of structural welds.

Across all of them, the inspector who writes a clear, defensible daily report is the one who keeps getting called back.

Choosing the Part C code for Las Vegas work

Part C is open book on one code of your choosing. AWS currently offers D1.1 (structural steel), API 1104 (pipelines), D1.2 (aluminum), D1.5 (bridges), D15.1 (railcars and locomotives), D17.1 (aerospace fusion welding), the ASME combination of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. In Southern Nevada the decision is usually simple:

Main line of workPart C bookNotes for Las Vegas candidates
Buildings, resorts, stadiums, data center frames, signs in steelAWS D1.1The default for almost all structural and special inspection work in the valley
Aluminum facades, canopies and sign structuresAWS D1.2Worth it only if aluminum is your daily material
Highway and pedestrian bridgesAWS D1.5For people working with bridge fabricators and transportation projects
Gas and utility pipelinesAPI 1104For pipeline construction and utility work
Power plant, central plant and process pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3For pipe welders and mechanical contractors

Seismic design is part of Southern Nevada structural work, and the seismic provisions sit in AISC 341 and the AWS D1.8 seismic supplement rather than in D1.1 alone. D1.8 is not a Part C option, but a D1.1 candidate who understands why demand-critical welds get extra attention will find the code questions easier. Use the D1.1 edition AWS names for the exam, which may be older than the one your project specifies. Background: AWS D1.1, D1.1 acceptance criteria and AWS D1.5.

The AWS Nevada Section and Southern Nevada welding schools

The AWS Nevada Section, part of AWS District 21, is the local section for Southern Nevada welders and inspectors. During 2025 it held its section meetings at the College of Southern Nevada's Henderson campus, with technical talks such as a session on the AWS Welding Handbook that earned attendees professional development hours, and it has held joint section meetings with ASNT in the past. Meetings are a good place to meet agency managers and fabricator QC leads, hear which projects are staffing up and line up people who can confirm your welding experience for the AWS application.

Many valley welders learned the trade at the College of Southern Nevada, which offers an Advanced Level Welder associate degree, an Entry-Level Welder certificate and shorter skills certificates in entry-level pipe welding, structural welding, weld manufacturing and gas tungsten arc welding. Its program covers shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, flux cored arc and gas tungsten arc welding, is recognized by AWS as a SENSE institution, and prepares graduates to test for AWS entry-level or advanced welder certification. Others came through union apprenticeships: the plumbers and pipefitters (UA Local 525) and the ironworkers (Local 433) both run apprenticeship programs in the valley. Recognized schooling can shorten the experience AWS requires for the CWI, and an apprenticeship record makes your work history easier to verify. These programs belong to the local training pipeline and are not connected to Atlantis.

Booking the CWI exam from Las Vegas

AWS QC1 (2016 edition, with its amendment) governs the examination, and each of the three parts needs a score of at least 72%. Part A asks 150 fundamentals questions. Part B combines hands-on tasks, using tools and specimens AWS hands you, with 46 questions. Part C is open book, about 50 to 65 questions on your selected code. Results arrive on a single consolidated score report.

Parts A and C are computer-based and booked with Prometric, using the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation letter, at a Prometric test center you choose. Part B is the part that may take you out of town. AWS runs the practical only at its own seminar and examination locations on its own dates, so check the current AWS schedule for the nearest session in the West and expect that it may mean a trip to another state. Book it early and around your project calendar. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org; for travel, time off and the other costs of the exam, see the CWI exam cost planner.

Studying around site hours and the desert summer

Construction in Las Vegas follows the heat. Summer crews often start before dawn to get the heavy work done early, and projects push hard toward milestones such as steel topping-out or a resort opening date. Special inspectors follow the contractors' hours, which can mean early starts one week and nights the next. The online format handles that: work through the fundamentals in the cooler months or quieter stretches, send questions to the instructor whenever your day allows, and keep the timed practice papers for the weeks just before your Prometric appointments.

For Part C, bring your D1.1 to site and look up the clauses behind the connections you are inspecting that day; finding prequalified joint details and visual acceptance criteria quickly is half the battle in the exam. For Part B, practise with fillet gauges, an undercut gauge and a bridge cam gauge on real welds until each reading is quick and certain. The Practical NDT welding workshop simulator adds browser practice on inspection steps when you are off site.

Corporate: six days at a Las Vegas contractor, fabricator or agency

Corporate delivery runs the full six days at the employer's own premises. For a fabricator that might be the shop floor and a meeting room beside it; for a special inspection agency, its office and lab. The practical day uses the company's own gauges and real welds, such as connection mock-ups, welder test plates and rejected production pieces, so measurement practice matches what those inspectors face on site. The code day centers on D1.1 and, where useful, the company's own procedures and inspection forms.

Timing usually works around the project calendar, for example between a steel package and the next mobilization. Each candidate still applies to AWS on their own, meets the eligibility and vision requirements on their own and books their own exam; an employer can support that but cannot submit it for them.

One-to-one sessions for a Las Vegas candidate

Under this format a single candidate gets six days of sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It suits an ironworker moving into QC who knows connections inside out but has never used a code book under time pressure, a field technician who needs the metallurgy and testing theory behind Part A, or a welder relocating to the valley who wants a credential that agencies recognize. Every session goes where that candidate needs it.

Eligibility and the vision record for Nevada applicants

How many years of welding-related experience AWS requires depends on education. A high school diploma means five years; a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology means one; trade courses and other qualifications fall in between, and less schooling means more years. The experience has to be verifiable work on welded products, such as fabrication, erection, repair or inspection, and AWS decides what qualifies. You also need an AWS Visual Acuity Record showing Jaeger J2 near vision at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, and a color perception test, completed by a qualified practitioner close enough to your exam date. If you do not yet have the years, the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) lets you start inspecting alongside a CWI. The full table is on the CWI exam prep course page, and the CWI requirements guide covers the rest.

After the CWI: career paths in Southern Nevada

A CWI is valid for nine years, with renewals at the third and sixth years and recertification at the ninth. In the Las Vegas market the next steps usually look like this.

  • Lead and senior inspection roles. Inspectors who run an agency's structural steel group or a fabricator's quality program often aim for the AWS Senior CWI; see the Senior CWI pathway. Some agencies also ask for ICC special inspector certifications, which ICC runs separately.
  • Ultrasonic and magnetic particle testing. Complete joint penetration welds in building and stadium steel are commonly checked by ultrasonic testing, and fillet welds by magnetic particle testing. Doing that work yourself needs method training, logged experience and certification by your employer under its written practice. Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; see NDT training in Las Vegas, UT Level 2, MT Level 2 and VT Level 2, and the Practical NDT page for Las Vegas.
  • Owner's representative work. Experienced CWIs move into owner-side roles on large projects, reviewing contractors' welding programs and fabricators' records.

To weigh the main inspection credentials against each other, read CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II and the CWI results by part. For structural steel consulting in the valley, see steel NDT consulting in Las Vegas.

Nearby CWI pages and a Las Vegas quote

Candidates elsewhere in the West can read the CWI exam prep pages for Phoenix, Salt Lake City, Los Angeles and San Francisco.

To price the course, tell us how many people want to prepare and in which format, outline each one's schooling and welding history, note the Part C book they plan to use, and for corporate delivery give the location, the gauges and sample welds available and the project dates to avoid. Use the Las Vegas CWI enquiry form.

faq.q: Does Atlantis have a CWI classroom in Las Vegas?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Las Vegas. Southern Nevada candidates take the six-day course online with an instructor answering questions, as one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking, or as a corporate course at their employer's facility. See the course outline.
AWS. It reviews applications, administers and scores the examination, and issues the CWI. The Atlantis course prepares candidates; AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed it.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits special inspection work in Las Vegas?
faq.a: AWS D1.1. Almost all structural steel on Las Vegas buildings, resorts, stadiums and data centers is welded to it, and it is what special inspectors work from day to day. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: Is a CWI required to work as a special inspector in Clark County?
faq.a: The building official approves special inspector qualifications, and Clark County approves the agencies that employ them. The CWI is not the only document involved, but agencies and fabricators commonly use it to show a person is qualified to inspect structural welding. Check with the agency you work for.

faq.q: Where do Las Vegas candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests booked through Prometric with the eligibility code from AWS. The practical, Part B, happens only at AWS-run sessions; Nevada candidates should look up the closest one in the West and be ready to travel for it.

faq.q: Can a special inspection agency have the six days run at its office?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings the course to your premises, uses your gauges and real welds, and keeps the code day on D1.1 and your own inspection forms. Each inspector still applies to AWS individually. Send an enquiry.

faq.q: Can I do the one-to-one format in person in Las Vegas?
faq.a: Yes. You can book all six one-to-one days in person, at a location agreed when you book, or take them online if that is easier around site hours. Atlantis has no venue in the city, so the place is arranged for each booking.

faq.q: Do the practice questions come from AWS exams?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes its own questions and timed papers, working from the subject areas AWS lists for each part. Nobody at Atlantis can see the AWS exam or its question bank.

faq.q: I am an ironworker. Does erection work count toward the experience requirement?
faq.a: It can, if it involved welding-related work on welded products, such as field welding, fit-up or inspection, and you can document it with dates, employers and someone who can verify it. AWS decides what counts; see CWI requirements.

faq.q: What can I add after the CWI to do ultrasonic testing of welds?
faq.a: Method training, logged experience and certification by your employer under its written practice. Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based training in UT, MT, PT and VT; see NDT training in Las Vegas and UT Level 2 training.
